comparison: Both evaluate autophagy induction claims (C5, C45, C48) and find them SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides more detailed analysis including C106, C107 and discusses multiple cell lines and controls. Peer reviewers describe evidence as 'solid' without detailed critique. Both accept the core autophagy induction findings.

Both evaluate synergy claims (C6, C51, C53, C55) and find them SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes exception in NCI-H358 cells (C52) and discusses methodology. Peer reviewers acknowledge synergistic effects without raising concerns. Strong agreement on in vitro synergy.

Partial overlap on claims C7 and C55 regarding in vivo tumor control. Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval discusses xenograft data in context of broader synergy analysis, while peer reviewers specifically highlight 'superior tumor control in vivo' as solid evidence.

Perfect claim overlap (C49, C50, C59, C60, C61, C62) regarding ULK1 inhibition validation. Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes concordance between pharmacological and genetic approaches strengthening on-target conclusions. Peer reviewers accept findings without critique as part of solid dataset.

Both evaluate GEM model efficacy claims (C8-C11, C81-C83) but reach different conclusions. OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED despite noting lack of statistical significance for combination. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, citing small sample size and lack of significant difference in tumor burden as critical concerns. Key disagreement on sufficiency of evidence.

Minimal overlap (C87 on toxicity). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval discusses weight loss as concerning negative finding tempering enthusiasm for combination. Peer reviewers acknowledge toxicity observations without specific concerns.

Strong overlap on histopathology claims (C88, C89, C141, C148, C149, C155) regarding ASC and mucinous adenocarcinoma enrichment. Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes mechanistic basis remains speculative. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge LKB1 deficiency diminishes sensitivity through emergence of these tumor types.

Strong overlap on KP model efficacy claims (C95, C96, C97). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes contrast with KL mice and lack of statistical significance for combination. Peer reviewers describe GEM model evidence as 'solid' and acknowledge differential response between models without critique.

Perfect claim overlap (C161-C165) on resistance mechanism. Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes clear mechanism (increased RAS/pERK) but questions clinical relevance of single cell line model. Peer reviewers accept findings as part of solid dataset without raising concerns about generalizability.

Partial overlap on GEM model characterization claims (C63-C67). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval discusses tumor burden and histopathological features. Peer reviewers describe GEM model evidence as 'solid' and accept characterization supporting experimental design.

Partial overlap on DCC-3116 single-agent activity claims (C124, C134, C139). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes activity is notable and somewhat unexpected, with mechanism not fully elucidated. Peer reviewers accept single-agent effects without questioning the findings.

Perfect claim overlap (C77, C78, C142, C144) on NKX2.1 retention findings. Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes this differs from prior models and suggests distinct lineage plasticity mechanisms. Peer reviewers accept molecular characterization without critique.

Perfect claim overlap (C56, C57, C92) on sotorasib pharmacodynamic validation. Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval describes as appropriate validation experiments. Peer reviewers treat as expected confirmatory data without questioning findings.

Partial overlap on molecular characterization claims (C68-C70). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval discusses pERK variability and low pAKT as important observations. Peer reviewers accept characterization as part of solid GEM model evidence base.

Minimal overlap (C47 on negative control). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes importance of KRASG12V control for specificity. Peer reviewers include C47 in overall acceptance of autophagy induction findings without specific discussion.

Minimal overlap (C107 on LKB1-independent autophagy). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval discusses C107 in context of multiple cell line validation. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge LKB1-independent autophagy induction as accepted finding.

OpenEval evaluates resistance model drug sensitivity claims (C111, C112) and finds them SUPPORTED, noting extreme trametinib sensitivity. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.

OpenEval evaluates background claims (C1-C4, C13-C16) about KRAS-driven lung cancer as SUPPORTED established knowledge. No corresponding peer review evaluation as these are contextual rather than novel findings.
OpenEval evaluates historical context claims (C17-C19) about KRASG12C inhibitor development as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation as these provide background context only.
OpenEval evaluates prior work claims (C20-C23) as SUPPORTED background. Peer review R6 touches on C23 regarding LKB1-independent effects but does not separately evaluate these historical claims.
OpenEval evaluates clinical context claims (C24-C26) about LKB1 deficiency as SUPPORTED established knowledge. No corresponding peer review evaluation as these are background claims.

OpenEval evaluates HCQ/CQ background claims (C28-C34) as SUPPORTED established knowledge providing rationale for selective inhibitors. No corresponding peer review evaluation of these contextual claims.
OpenEval evaluates autophagy biology background claims (C37-C42) as SUPPORTED established knowledge. No corresponding peer review evaluation as these provide necessary background only.

OpenEval evaluates clinical trial information claims (C43, C44, C129) as SUPPORTED factual information about translational potential. No corresponding peer review evaluation of these contextual claims.
OpenEval evaluates clinical knowledge claims (C156-C158) about ASC as SUPPORTED background context. No corresponding peer review evaluation as these are established knowledge claims.

Peer reviewers evaluate LKB1-independent autophagy and treatment sensitivity claims (C23, C107, C121) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval addresses these claims separately in R1 (C107) and R18 (C23), but not as a unified evaluation of the LKB1-independence finding.
